title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 136 (Right of member to copies of audited financial statements)

content.overview: Section 136 requires a copy of the financial statements, including consolidated statements, the auditor's report and every other document required to be annexed, to be sent to every member, every trustee for the debenture-holders, and all other persons entitled, not less than twenty-one days before the meeting.
content.glance: A copy of the financial statements, including consolidated statements, the auditor's report and other documents, must be sent to every member, trustee for debenture holders and other persons entitled, not less than twenty-one days before the meeting.
content.study:
## Statutory rule
Section 136(1) requires a copy of the financial statements, including consolidated financial statements, if any, auditor's report and every other document required by law to be annexed or attached to the financial statements, which are to be laid before a company in its general meeting, to be sent to every member of the company, to every trustee for the debenture-holders, and to all persons so entitled, not less than twenty-one days before the date of the meeting.

The provisos allow a shorter period if agreed, and a listed company to send a statement containing the salient features in the prescribed form.

Section 136(2) keeps a copy at the registered office for inspection during business hours.

## Answer structure
Twenty-one days, to members and debenture trustees. A listed company may use the prescribed statement of salient features. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Listed companies and companies with a website may use the circulation modes the section permits. A member may obtain a copy on request. The statements are laid before the annual general meeting under section 129 and filed under section 137.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: A properly incorporated company was challenged as indistinct from its controlling shareholder.
cases.issue: What is the legal effect of incorporation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A registered company is a legal person separate from its members, even when control and ownership are concentrated.
cases.holding: The company's separate personality was affirmed.
cases.relevance: Use for Companies Act s. 9 and corporate personality.

cases.name: Foss v. Harbottle
cases.facts: Shareholders sought relief for alleged wrongs to the company.
cases.issue: Who may sue for a wrong done to the company and when may exceptions apply?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The company is the proper plaintiff for corporate wrongs, subject to recognised exceptions such as fraud on the minority and ultra vires acts.
cases.holding: The proper-plaintiff and majority-rule principles were established.
cases.relevance: Use with oppression, mismanagement and class-action analysis.

cases.name: Needle Industries (India) Ltd. v. Needle Industries Newey (India) Holding Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court examined share issue powers and alleged oppression.
cases.issue: When does a corporate action become oppressive or invalid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court examines purpose, fairness, statutory power and resulting prejudice rather than treating every irregularity as oppression.
cases.holding: The corporate action was assessed under the statutory and equitable framework.
cases.relevance: Use for share allotment and oppression claims.

cases.name: Miheer H. Mafatlal v. Mafatlal Industries Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court reviewed a scheme of arrangement sanctioned by the company court.
cases.issue: What is the court's role in sanctioning a corporate scheme?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The court must ensure statutory compliance, class fairness, informed approval and absence of illegality, but does not substitute its commercial judgment for the company's decision.
cases.holding: The principles governing scheme sanction were stated.
cases.relevance: Use for corporate arrangements and tribunal scrutiny.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 136 (Right of member to copies of audited financial statements). A copy of the financial statements, including consolidated statements, the auditor's report and other documents, must be sent to every member, trustee for debenture holders and other persons entitled, not less than twenty-one days before the meeting. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.
